title: The Oil Towns to the Bunkers: the Forty-Third President, the Third Generation, and the War He Ordered
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Union Bank and the Oil Towns

stops.name: New York, the Union Banking Corporation seized
stops.date_confidence: attested; the seizure date comes from prescott_bush.journey.json and QUEUE.md line 245, and the coordinates are inherited from that file unchanged
stops.campa: Four years before the boy is born, the United States government seizes the Union Banking Corporation under the Trading with the Enemy Act. Prescott Bush sits on its board. The atlas already holds this room, under the grandfather's name, and the family file states the line as running forward from him through the father to the third generation. Wall Street pays the family and Washington employs it, and for the next sixty years the house treats the two as one address. The grandson inherits the name before he inherits anything else.
suggested_refs: The 1942 Trading with the Enemy Act seizure order against the Union Banking Corporation

stops.name: New Haven, birth at Grace-New Haven
stops.date_confidence: attested; coordinates corrected from the geography lens, which gave 41.3033, -72.9407, some 380 m west of the hospital
stops.campa: George Walker Bush is born at Grace-New Haven Community Hospital on the sixth of July, first of the six children of George H. W. Bush and Barbara Pierce Bush. His father, a Navy pilot four years out of the Pacific, is finishing a Yale degree in two and a half years and playing first base for the college. The city the son is born in he will return to at eighteen as a student and never live in again. Everything the name carries is Connecticut. Everything he will later claim as his own is Texas.
suggested_refs: Grace-New Haven Community Hospital, so named 1945 to 1965, now Yale New Haven Hospital

stops.name: Midland, the boy in the boom town
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the family reaches Texas in 1948, lives at Odessa 1948 to 1950, and the Midland years run to 1959, so the day and month here are conventional
stops.campa: The family comes to the Permian Basin in 1948 for the oil, to Odessa first and then to Midland, a flat town of new houses raised on wells and on the expectation of more wells. Here the eastern accent goes. He plays Little League on caliche fields and learns the vocabulary of leases and dry holes early. The manner he takes from the town will read in Texas as ordinary and in Washington as a costume put on. Midland is where the family's second fortune is dug out of the ground, and where his own attempt at one will fail.
suggested_refs: The house at 1412 West Ohio Avenue, Midland, opened as the George W. Bush Childhood Home museum on 11 April 2006

stops.name: Memorial Sloan-Kettering, New York, the sister
stops.date_confidence: attested; the geography lens wrongly attached this death to the Midland pin, and the correction places the treatment and death in New York
stops.campa: Pauline Robinson Bush, called Robin, is three years old when a Midland doctor finds leukemia in her blood. Her parents fly her to New York and to Memorial Sloan-Kettering, where the treatments of 1953 buy months and not years. She dies on the eleventh of October. George is seven. He is not told his sister is ill until after she is dead, and in the same week he learns that his mother has stopped laughing and that the work of making her start again has fallen to him. In 2000 Robin is moved from Connecticut to the library grounds at College Station, where both her parents will follow.
suggested_refs: Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center, New York, where Robin Bush was treated and died

stops.name: Walker's Point, Kennebunkport, the summers
stops.date_confidence: attested for the family's tenure; the pin is inherited byte-identical from prescott_bush.journey.json, and the geography lens's 43.3272, -70.4051 is discarded as it falls 4.7 km out in open water
stops.campa: On a granite finger running into the Atlantic north of Kennebunkport stands the house the Walker and Bush families have kept since the twenties. Every summer of the boy's childhood is spent here: cold water, the speedboat, horseshoes, three generations at one long table. It is the one address the family never has to explain to anybody. He will bring heads of government to these rocks as president and clear no brush on them. Prescott Bush stands on this same point in the atlas already, and the father and the grandson keep the house after him.
suggested_refs: Walker's Point Estate, Kennebunkport, held by the family from the 1920s
sources: George H. W. Bush Presidential Library materials

stops.name: Yale University, the fraternity and the tomb
stops.date_confidence: attested for the years 1964 to 1968; the day and month are the conventional start of term
stops.campa: He goes east to Andover first, his father's school, where he is a middling student and head cheerleader for the baseball team, and then to Yale, his father's university and his grandfather's. He reads history, presides over Delta Kappa Epsilon, and is tapped for Skull and Bones as both of them were before him. The class of 1968 graduates into the Tet Offensive. Nothing at Yale is his by achievement and nothing there is denied him, and he leaves the place disliking it. The dislike will be worth votes in Texas for the rest of his life.
suggested_refs: Phillips Academy, Andover, 1961 to 1964, at 42.6473, -71.1316

segments.name: The Guard, the Wells, the Fortieth Birthday

stops.name: Ellington Field, Houston, the enlistment
stops.date_confidence: attested; the chronology lens's 'joined the United States Air Force and was commissioned into the Texas Air National Guard' is a compression of Guard accession procedure and is corrected here, and the geography lens's placing of F-102 training at Moody is corrected to Ellington
stops.campa: Twelve days before his Yale degree he enlists in the Texas Air National Guard at Ellington and is commissioned second lieutenant. He never serves in the regular Air Force; the accession is Guard from the first day. Fifty-four weeks of undergraduate pilot training follow at Moody Air Force Base in Georgia on the T-37 and the T-38, and then he comes back to Ellington and the combat crew training school of the 147th, soloing the F-102 interceptor in March 1970 and graduating that June. The waiting lists for Guard flying slots that year run to years. His does not.
suggested_refs: Texas Air National Guard service records released in 2004

stops.name: Dannelly Field, Montgomery, the Alabama drills
stops.date_confidence: attested for the transfer and the suspension in 1972; the day and month are conventional, the coordinates are supplied by this compilation rather than by the pool, and the unit is styled 187th Fighter Wing in one source and 187th Tactical Reconnaissance Group in period usage, not resolved
stops.campa: He asks for a transfer to Alabama to work on a Senate campaign and is attached to the 187th at Montgomery. In August he is suspended from flying status for failing to take the required annual physical, and the F-102 he trained on is being retired from the inventory in any case. Whether he appeared for drills in Montgomery that autumn is the question that will be put to him in the campaign of 2004, and the paper trail is thin enough on both sides that neither the accusation nor the denial ever closes. He is honorably discharged in November 1974.
suggested_refs: The 2004 dispute over the Alabama drill records and the Killian documents, unresolved in the sources reachable here

stops.name: Harvard Business School, Boston, the MBA
stops.date_confidence: attested for the degree in 1975; the day and month are the conventional start of term, and the geography lens's 'first US president to hold one' is corrected to 'only', which is what the chronology lens says
stops.campa: He is admitted to Harvard Business School and takes the degree in 1975, the only president of the United States who holds one. Classmates remember a man in a flight jacket chewing tobacco in a room of pressed shirts. What he carries out of Cambridge is not finance. It is a vocabulary of delegation, and a settled preference for the decision over the deliberation that produced it. He goes back to Midland the same year to drill for oil with other people's money.
suggested_refs: Harvard Business School class of 1975 records

stops.name: Midland, the marriage and Arbusto
stops.date_confidence: attested for the marriage; the Harken absorption of Spectrum 7 is dated 1986 here on the correction, against the chronology lens's 1987, and that disagreement is not silently closed
stops.campa: He meets Laura Welch, a school librarian, at a backyard barbecue in July and marries her in Midland in November, a courtship of a few months. The same year he founds Arbusto Energy, which is Spanish for bush, and raises money for it from his father's friends. The wells come in dry more often than they come in wet. Arbusto becomes Spectrum 7 in 1984 with him as chairman, Harken Energy absorbs Spectrum 7 for two hundred thousand shares, and he takes a seat on the Harken board. Every failure in the sequence is absorbed by somebody else's balance sheet.
suggested_refs: SEC filings for Arbusto Energy, Spectrum 7 and Harken Energy Corporation

stops.name: Lubbock, the race against Kent Hance
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1978 defeat; the coordinates are supplied by this compilation as the principal city of the nineteenth district, the pool having named no pin
stops.campa: He runs for the open House seat in the nineteenth district of Texas, a run of cotton and oil country across the Panhandle plains, and loses to the Democrat Kent Hance by six points. Hance runs him as a Yale and Harvard man playing at being a West Texan, and the charge sticks to him. He will not stand for office again for sixteen years, and when he does he will hold the ground to his right and answer the charge of being an eastern man before an opponent can make it.
suggested_refs: The 1978 general election in Texas's nineteenth congressional district

stops.name: Colorado Springs, the fortieth birthday
stops.date_confidence: attested for July 1986 and the fortieth birthday; the Broadmoor coordinates are supplied by this compilation, the pool having named the city only
stops.campa: He turns forty in Colorado Springs with Laura and friends, drinks through the night, and wakes with a decision made. He stops that day and never resumes. He will describe it afterward not as an intervention and not as a diagnosis but as the end of a habit of selfishness, and he will date his life in two halves from that morning. The twin daughters born in Dallas in November 1981, Barbara and Jenna, named for their grandmothers, are four years old. Within two years he is in Washington working his father's presidential campaign.
suggested_refs: The Broadmoor hotel, Colorado Springs, site of the fortieth birthday weekend

stops.name: Arlington, the Rangers bought
stops.date_confidence: attested for April 1989 and the eighty-nine million dollar purchase; the personal stake is given as five hundred thousand dollars by the chronology lens and eight hundred thousand by the source it cites, so no figure is stated here
stops.campa: He assembles an investor group that buys the Texas Rangers for eighty-nine million dollars and takes the title of managing general partner. He sits in the stands with the crowd rather than in a box, and his name goes on the trades. The team plays at Arlington Stadium, and he spends five years securing public money for the ballpark that replaces it in 1994. The oil years never made him famous. Five seasons of baseball make him known in Texas under his own name rather than his father's. The coordinates here are the new ballpark's, not the old one's.
suggested_refs: Arlington Stadium, the Rangers' ground until 1993, and the Ballpark in Arlington, opened April 1994

stops.name: Panama City, the father's war on the asset
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pin is inherited byte-identical from manuel_noriega.journey.json and william_casey.journey.json
stops.campa: Twenty thousand American troops land in Panama and take the country inside a week in order to arrest its head of state. Manuel Noriega has been on the CIA payroll since before George H. W. Bush ran the agency in 1976, was inherited by William Casey under Reagan, and was kept there until he was worth more deposed than employed. The father sets the sequence in that week: an asset is declared a monster and removed by invasion, and the invasion is popular at home. Fourteen years later the son orders the same thing done in Baghdad.
suggested_refs: Operation Just Cause, December 1989, and the CIA payroll relationship traced in the Noriega and Casey files

stops.name: Kuwait City, the Seif Palace
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pin is inherited byte-identical from saddam_hussein.journey.json
stops.campa: Iraqi armor crosses the frontier before dawn and Saddam Hussein's men take the Seif Palace on the waterfront. The father assembles a coalition of dozens of countries, drives the Iraqi army out of Kuwait in a hundred hours, and stops at the border rather than march on Baghdad. In the family telling that decision not to finish it costs the father a second term, and it leaves the son an unfinished war with a named enemy who survives, still in his own palaces, for twelve more years.
suggested_refs: The Seif Palace, Kuwait City, taken on the first morning of the 1990 invasion

stops.name: Austin, sworn in as governor
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He unseats Ann Richards with 53.5 percent of the vote by refusing every provocation she offers him and running on four subjects and nothing else. Sworn in as the forty-sixth governor of Texas, he works across the aisle with the Democratic lieutenant governor Bob Bullock, signs tort reform and school accountability into law, and presides over a record number of executions. In 1998 he is returned with 68 percent, the largest margin in the state's history, and in the same year sells his Rangers shares at a profit of some fifteen million dollars.
suggested_refs: The Texas Governor's Mansion, Austin, occupied 1995 to 2000

stops.name: Crawford, Prairie Chapel Ranch
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1999 purchase; the day and month are conventional, and the coordinates are corrected from the geography lens's 31.6621, -97.3811, which sat some 19 km away
stops.campa: He buys fifteen hundred and eighty-three acres of scrub, cedar and limestone canyon outside Crawford, an hour from Austin, and builds a low limestone house on it. The ranch is bought the year before the presidential run. Kennebunkport is the grandfather's Atlantic. This is his own dirt, and he will clear brush on it in front of cameras for eight years. Vladimir Putin comes here, and Tony Blair, and the diplomacy of the boots and the pickup truck is conducted from a house that has no formal rooms in it.
suggested_refs: Prairie Chapel Ranch, Crawford, Texas, purchased 1999

segments.name: The Recount and the Morning of the Eleventh

stops.name: Washington, the Supreme Court decides
stops.date_confidence: attested; the chronology lens dated Bush v. Gore to 9 December, which was the stay halting the recount, while the case was argued 11 December and decided 12 December
stops.campa: Five hundred and thirty-seven votes in Florida separate two men on the night of the seventh of November, and thirty-five days of punch cards, hanging chads and county courthouses follow. On the ninth of December the Supreme Court stays the recount. On the twelfth it decides Bush v. Gore, five to four, and the recount does not resume. He takes the presidency with 271 electoral votes to Al Gore's 266 while losing the popular vote by 543,895. No man has entered the office on those terms since 1888, and half the country will not concede the result at all.
suggested_refs: Bush v. Gore, 531 U.S. 98, argued 11 December and decided 12 December 2000

stops.name: United States Capitol, the inauguration
stops.date_confidence: attested; No Child Left Behind is dated to its signing on 8 January 2002 here, against the chronology lens's 2001, which is the year Congress passed it
stops.campa: He is sworn in as the forty-third president on the west front of the Capitol in cold rain, with Dick Cheney beside him, chosen in July to run the search for a running mate and then chosen as the running mate. His first year is domestic and narrow in ambition: a tax cut of 1.35 trillion dollars, an education bill he will sign in January 2002 as No Child Left Behind, and a foreign policy stated explicitly against nation-building. He is a president elected to do very little abroad, and he has eight months left of that presidency.
suggested_refs: The first inaugural address, 20 January 2001, White House archives

stops.name: Emma E. Booker Elementary School, Sarasota, the seven minutes
stops.date_confidence: attested; coordinates corrected from 27.3364, -82.5307, which both the geography and the afterlife lens carried and which sits 2.4 km southwest of the school
stops.campa: He is sitting with second-graders when Andrew Card leans to his ear and says that a second plane has hit the second tower and America is under attack. He does not stand. For roughly seven minutes he stays in the small chair in front of the children with the book open in his hands. The footage of those minutes becomes the most argued-over film of the presidency, read as paralysis by some and as composure by others, and neither reading has ever won. He leaves the school at half past nine.
suggested_refs: The classroom footage from Emma E. Booker Elementary, 11 September 2001

stops.name: Offutt Air Force Base, the bunker
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Air Force One flies west and south all day with fighter escort and no announced destination: Barksdale in Louisiana first, where he records a brief statement to a camera, and then Offutt in Nebraska, down into the underground command post of United States Strategic Command, built to fight a nuclear war against a state. He convenes the National Security Council by secure video from a bunker designed for an enemy he does not have. That evening he insists on flying back to Washington against advice and speaks to the country from the Oval Office.
suggested_refs: The USSTRATCOM underground command post at Offutt, used on the afternoon of 11 September 2001

stops.name: World Trade Center site, the bullhorn
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Three days later he stands on the crushed roof of a fire engine in the smoke at the pile, his arm around a retired firefighter, and when the crowd shouts that it cannot hear him he answers through the bullhorn. The same day he speaks at Washington National Cathedral before four living presidents and declares the war from the pulpit. His approval goes to ninety percent, the highest ever recorded for the office. In January half the country called the election stolen and the man in it illegitimate.
stops.quote: I can hear you, the rest of the world hears you, and the people who knocked these buildings down will hear all of us soon.
stops.quote_source: George W. Bush at the World Trade Center site, 14 September 2001, White House Archives transcript
suggested_refs: The bullhorn and the fire engine from Ground Zero, 14 September 2001, now museum objects

stops.name: United Nations Headquarters, the challenge to the hall
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: At West Point in June he told the graduating cadets that deterrence and containment no longer hold and that the United States will strike first against threats still forming, and the doctrine takes his name. In September he carries it to the General Assembly and tells the United Nations that it must enforce its own resolutions against Iraq or accept its own irrelevance. Kofi Annan will still be repeating that sentence sixteen years later, in the last interviews of his life. Resolution 1441 passes unanimously in November and the inspectors go back in.
suggested_refs: The West Point commencement address of 1 June 2002 and UN Security Council Resolution 1441
sources: CNBC, 'Kofi Annan, former UN secretary general, dies aged 80', 18 August 2018

stops.name: Cincinnati Museum Center, the grave and gathering danger
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In a converted railway terminal in Ohio, days before Congress votes on the war authorization, he sets out the case: aluminum tubes, mobile weapons laboratories, unmanned aircraft, an Iraq that could put chemical weapons into the hands of terrorists on a day of its own choosing. The House votes 296 to 133 three days later and the Senate 77 to 23. Of the specific claims made in this hall, most will not survive inspection of the country the speech is about, and the phrase at its center will outlive every one of them.
stops.quote_source: George W. Bush, address at the Cincinnati Museum Center, 7 October 2002, White House Archives transcript
suggested_refs: The Cincinnati address of 7 October 2002 and the congressional authorization that followed it

stops.name: Marseille, lunch with Richard Perle
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; the day and month default to the first, and the pin is inherited byte-identical from adnan_khashoggi.journey.json
stops.campa: In the year the invasion is launched, Adnan Khashoggi takes lunch in Marseille with Richard Perle, chairman of the Defense Policy Board that advises the Bush Pentagon and among the loudest voices for removing Saddam Hussein. The arms broker who moved American weapons toward Iran under Reagan and the theorist of the coming war sit at one table while the war is still being argued in Washington. The atlas has Khashoggi's path already, and it crosses the president's here, at a lunch the president is not at and does not know about.
suggested_refs: The Defense Policy Board under Richard Perle, 2001 to 2003

stops.name: Lajes Field, Azores, the last summit
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On a wind-scoured American air base in the middle of the Atlantic he meets Tony Blair, Jose Maria Aznar and Jose Manuel Barroso for a summit lasting under two hours. There is nothing left in it to negotiate: the second resolution is dead in the Security Council and the meeting exists to give the ultimatum a stage and three other faces. The next evening he gives Saddam Hussein and his sons forty-eight hours to leave Iraq. The island lies a thousand miles from any capital in the coalition, and the summit is held on an American base on it.
suggested_refs: The Azores summit of 16 March 2003 at Lajes Field, Terceira

stops.name: Baghdad, the bunkers under the invasion
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pin is inherited byte-identical from saddam_hussein.journey.json
stops.campa: Cruise missiles open on a compound south of the city before dawn, fired on an intelligence report that Saddam Hussein is sleeping there. He is not. For three weeks the coalition drives north from Kuwait while the man they came for moves between bunkers under his own capital, issuing orders to an army dissolving around him. The atlas records these same weeks from underneath, in Saddam Hussein's file, where the war has no air support and no maps. From above it is the war the president ordered on the argument he made in Cincinnati.
suggested_refs: The opening strike of 20 March 2003 and the Iraqi leadership bunkers beneath Baghdad

stops.name: Firdos Square, the statue comes down
stops.date_confidence: attested for the event; the pin is inherited byte-identical from saddam_hussein.journey.json, and the geography lens's 33.3081, 44.3806 is discarded as 4.2 km west of the square. The size and spontaneity of the crowd remain contested
stops.campa: A Marine recovery vehicle puts a chain around the neck of a bronze Saddam Hussein in a square in Karrada, and a small crowd of Iraqis beats the fallen head with their shoes while the cameras of the hotel opposite carry it live. The image goes round the world inside an hour as the fall of the regime. Later examination of the wide shots shows a square mostly empty and a crowd of a few dozen men, and the reading of that afternoon has been argued ever since. The president is nine thousand kilometers away, and the picture is his.
suggested_refs: The wide-angle photographs of Firdos Square, 9 April 2003, and the later analyses of the crowd

stops.name: USS Abraham Lincoln, the banner
stops.date_confidence: attested; the chronology lens tagged this a reconstruction with the date unconfirmed, which is wrong, and the two lenses gave two positions, 32.64, -117.17 and 32.7, -117.6, of which the latter is used as the carrier was roughly thirty miles offshore
stops.campa: He lands on the deck of a carrier some thirty miles off the California coast in the right-hand seat of a Navy S-3B, steps out in a flight suit, and delivers the speech beneath a banner reading Mission Accomplished that the ship's crew is later said to have hung. The war he declares finished has six more years of American fighting in it and will kill most of its dead after this afternoon. The landing and the flight suit are his own staff's arrangement, and the photographs of that afternoon are used against him for the rest of the presidency.
stops.quote: Major combat operations in Iraq have ended.
stops.quote_source: George W. Bush aboard USS Abraham Lincoln, 1 May 2003, White House Archives transcript
suggested_refs: The Mission Accomplished banner and the flight-suit photographs of 1 May 2003

segments.name: The World Tour of the War President

stops.name: Baghdad International Airport, the Thanksgiving turkey
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Air Force One comes into Baghdad in darkness with its lights out, the press aboard sworn to silence and the flight logged as a movement to Crawford. He spends a little over two hours on the ground in a mess hall carrying a roast turkey on a platter to six hundred soldiers who did not know he was in the hemisphere. The turkey is a display piece and not the meal, which is a detail the photographs do not carry and the later reporting does. He is in the air again before the city knows he came.
suggested_refs: The secret Thanksgiving visit of 27 November 2003, kept from the press until the aircraft was homebound

stops.name: Ad-Dawr, the spider hole
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pin is inherited byte-identical from saddam_hussein.journey.json
stops.campa: Eight months into the war, soldiers of the Fourth Infantry Division pull Saddam Hussein out of a covered hole two meters deep beside a mud hut near Ad-Dawr, bearded and filthy, with a pistol he does not draw, a great deal of American cash, and two men for a bodyguard. Paul Bremer announces it in Baghdad the next day. In Washington the president is told at dawn and asks for confirmation twice before he will believe it. The atlas holds this hole in Saddam Hussein's file. It is the one clean ending the war produces.
suggested_refs: The spider hole at Ad-Dawr, 13 December 2003

stops.name: Tripoli, the weapons renounced
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pin is inherited byte-identical from muammar_gaddafi.journey.json
stops.campa: Six days after the hole at Ad-Dawr, Muammar Gaddafi announces that Libya will surrender its chemical weapons and its nuclear program to international inspection, after nine months of secret talks with London and Washington that opened in the week the invasion did. The administration presents it as the dividend of the war and as the demonstration that force at Baghdad buys disarmament at Tripoli. Eight years later the man who disarmed is killed in a drainage pipe by a coalition that no longer has any weapons to fear from him.
suggested_refs: Libya's 19 December 2003 declaration and the dismantling of its weapons programs

stops.name: Baghdad Green Zone, the first appearance
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pin is inherited byte-identical from saddam_hussein.journey.json, whose own text names only 'the American president' and leaves the identification to the date, while the quote itself names Bush outright
stops.campa: Brought before an Iraqi judge in a room in the Green Zone, unshaven and in a jacket without a tie, the former president of Iraq refuses to recognize the court and asks the judge by what authority he sits. Asked to identify himself he answers that the judge is an Iraqi and knows perfectly well who he is. The tribunal exists because of an invasion ordered by a president who is not in the room, is not named in the indictment, and is named anyway, by the defendant, in the first minutes of the first hearing.
stops.quote: This is all theater. The real criminal is Bush
stops.quote_source: Saddam Hussein, first hearing before the Iraqi Special Tribunal, 1 July 2004, as translated and reported
suggested_refs: The video record of the first hearing before the Iraqi Special Tribunal, 1 July 2004

stops.name: Freedom Square, Tbilisi, the grenade
stops.date_confidence: attested; the grenade was confirmed live by later investigation and was not disclosed at the time
stops.campa: He addresses a hundred and fifty thousand Georgians in Freedom Square on the freedom agenda that is now the whole content of his second inaugural, and calls their Rose Revolution a beacon to the region. While he is speaking a live Soviet-made grenade lands within some tens of meters of the podium, wrapped in a cloth that keeps the striker lever from releasing. It does not go off. The crowd is not told, the president is not told for hours, and the device is confirmed live by investigators only weeks afterward.
suggested_refs: The 10 May 2005 Tbilisi grenade, recovered from Freedom Square and confirmed live by the FBI

stops.name: Jackson Square, New Orleans, the lit cathedral
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Seventeen days after the levees fail and a city of half a million is emptied by water, he stands lit by generators in front of the cathedral in Jackson Square and pledges the federal government to rebuild the Gulf Coast. The audience is a square with no residents left in it. He has already been photographed at the window of Air Force One looking down on the flooded city from three thousand feet, and has already told the head of FEMA he was doing a fine job. His approval never returns to where it stood on the twenty-eighth of August.
suggested_refs: The Jackson Square address of 15 September 2005 and the Air Force One flyover photograph of 31 August

stops.name: Caracas, Mr. Danger
stops.date_confidence: attested for a nationally televised speech in March 2006; the day defaults to the first, and the quote is printed with ellipses because the pool had welded separated passages into one contiguous block
stops.campa: From a stage in Caracas the president of Venezuela addresses the president of the United States directly, in the second person, at length, on national television, and does it again and again for three years running. Mr. Danger is his standing name for the man. The Bush administration answers by declining to answer. Oil keeps moving from Venezuelan wells to American refineries at a rate neither government interrupts for a day. The speeches on both sides are arranged around that trade.
stops.quote: You messed up with me, birdie... You are a donkey, Mr. Danger... You are a coward, you know? You are a coward... Coward, assassin, genocidal... You are an alcoholic, a drunk... You are immoral, Mr. Danger... The worst of this planet, the very worst is called George W. Bush.
stops.quote_source: Hugo Chavez, nationally televised speech, March 2006, translated from Spanish, quoted on Wikiquote; ellipses mark the joins between separated passages
suggested_refs: The Wikiquote entries for Hugo Chavez and George W. Bush, which mirror the same March 2006 passage

stops.name: United Nations Headquarters, the smell of sulphur
stops.date_confidence: attested; the quote lens carried this passage twice, once dated 21 September, and the correct date is 20 September, the morning after Bush addressed the same rostrum. The official UN English translation is used here in place of the press rendering
stops.campa: He addresses the General Assembly on the nineteenth of September. The next morning Hugo Chavez takes the same rostrum, crosses himself, holds up a book by Noam Chomsky and tells the hall what the podium smells like. The chamber laughs and then applauds. Five years earlier this president stood at ninety percent approval and four living presidents sat behind him in a cathedral. His father built a coalition of thirty-five nations out of this room. It is the same room.
stops.quote: The Devil came here yesterday, right here. It still smells of sulphur today. Yesterday on this rostrum the President of the United States, whom I refer to as the Devil, talked as if he owned the world.
stops.quote_source: Hugo Chavez, address to the UN General Assembly, 20 September 2006, official UN English translation, A/61/PV.12
suggested_refs: UN General Assembly verbatim record A/61/PV.12, 20 September 2006
sources: Wikisource, 'Address to the United Nations General Assembly (Chávez, 2006-09-20)'
es.wikisource.org, 'Discurso del Presidente Hugo Chávez en la Asamblea General de la ONU de 2006'

stops.name: Camp Justice, Kadhimiya, the rope
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pin is inherited byte-identical from saddam_hussein.journey.json
stops.campa: Saddam Hussein is hanged before dawn on the first day of Eid in a former military intelligence building in Kadhimiya, taunted on the scaffold by his guards, the whole of it filmed on a mobile telephone and on the internet within hours. The Iraqi government carries out the sentence of a tribunal established under the occupation the president ordered. He is asleep at Crawford and is not woken for it. He says afterward that the execution looked to him like a revenge killing rather than an act of justice.
suggested_refs: The mobile-telephone footage of the execution, 30 December 2006

stops.name: Al Asad Airbase, Anbar, the surge reviewed
stops.date_confidence: attested; the geography lens named Anbar in its text but pinned Al Faw Palace in Baghdad, an internal contradiction, and the coordinates here are carried at the two decimals the correction supplies and not falsely extended
stops.campa: He flies unannounced into Anbar province, a hundred miles west of Baghdad, with Condoleezza Rice, Robert Gates and Peter Pace, to sit with the tribal sheikhs of the Awakening in the province American commanders had written off as lost eighteen months before. The surge of thirty thousand troops he announced in January is holding, and this visit is its advertisement, staged in Anbar rather than in the capital because Anbar is the part of the country that is working. Six days later Petraeus reports to Congress.
suggested_refs: The Anbar Awakening and the surprise presidential visit of 3 September 2007

stops.name: Bucharest, what Putin says about Ukraine
stops.date_confidence: attested for the remark and the summit; the closed-session character of the exchange means the wording rests on the reporting rather than on a transcript
stops.campa: At the NATO summit in Bucharest he pushes for membership action plans for Ukraine and Georgia and is blocked by Germany and France. In a closed session Vladimir Putin tells him what he considers Ukraine to be. Four months later Russian armor is in South Ossetia, and Putin is telling Nicolas Sarkozy by telephone what he intends to do to the Georgian president, adding by way of precedent that the Americans hanged Saddam Hussein. The man who called Tbilisi a beacon from its own main square does not intervene.
stops.quote: You do understand, George, that Ukraine is not even a state. What is Ukraine? Part of its territories is Eastern Europe, but the greater part is a gift from us.
stops.quote_source: Vladimir Putin to George W. Bush, NATO Bucharest Summit, 4 April 2008, translated from Russian, cited in Time
suggested_refs: The Bucharest summit communique of April 2008 and the August 2008 Russo-Georgian war
sources: Le Nouvel Observateur and The Telegraph, 13 November 2008

stops.name: Washington, the farewell address
stops.date_confidence: attested and primary; the chronology lens tagged this a reconstruction with the date unconfirmed, and it is a dated White House release, 20090115-17
stops.campa: Five days before he goes, he speaks to the country for the last time from the East Room, with a recession fourteen months old, a financial system standing on seven hundred billion dollars of emergency money he signed for in October, and approval figures in the twenties. He asks to be judged on a thing that did not happen, which is a second attack on American soil. The two wars are unfinished and pass to his successor entire, together with the longest recession since the Second World War.
suggested_refs: White House release 20090115-17, 'President Bush Delivers Farewell Address to the Nation'

stops.name: Andrews Air Force Base, the departure
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He watches Barack Obama sworn in on the same west front where he took the oath twice, then walks with Laura to the helicopter on the east lawn, which flies a slow circle over the Capitol before setting down at Andrews. The aircraft that is Air Force One while he is aboard reverts at noon to a call sign that is only a number. He flies to Midland and speaks to a crowd in the town where he grew up, and goes on to Dallas the same night, out of office at sixty-two.
suggested_refs: The departure ceremony at Andrews and the Midland homecoming rally of 20 January 2009

stops.name: Preston Hollow, Dallas, the silence and the brushes
stops.date_confidence: attested for the move; the start of the painting practice is soft in every source, given only as around 2012
stops.campa: He and Laura settle in a house on a cul-de-sac in north Dallas, and he begins a public silence he keeps for years, declining almost every invitation to comment on his successor. He writes Decision Points, published in 2010. Around 2012 he takes up oil painting, self-taught first and then studying with instructors, working from photographs: dogs, the world leaders he negotiated with, and then the wounded veterans of the wars he ordered, sixty-six of whose portraits are published in 2017 for the benefit of the Military Service Initiative.
suggested_refs: Portraits of Courage: A Commander in Chief's Tribute to America's Warriors, Crown, 28 February 2017
sources: Crown Publishing and Bush Institute release materials

stops.name: Southern Methodist University, the center dedicated
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool gave three different coordinates for this one building, 32.8459/-96.7813 and 32.8437/-96.7811 and the correct 32.8409/-96.7781, and the last is used
stops.campa: On the campus of Southern Methodist University he dedicates the library, the museum and the policy institute that will hold his papers and make his case, with Obama, Clinton, Carter and his father on the platform beside him. The museum's central exhibit is a room called Decision Points Theater, in which a visitor is handed the intelligence he was handed and asked what they would have done with it. Everything a presidency leaves behind is here except a grave. He is sixty-six years old and this atlas has no tomb to record.
suggested_refs: The George W. Bush Presidential Center at SMU, dedicated 25 April 2013

stops.name: College Station, the father in the ground
stops.date_confidence: attested; coordinates corrected from the afterlife lens's 30.6046, -96.3521. The direction of the candy passed at the McCain funeral is contradicted between sources and is left unstated here
stops.campa: His father is buried on the grounds of the George Bush Presidential Library at Texas A&M, beside Barbara, laid there in April, and beside Robin, moved from Connecticut in 2000 to lie with them. The son delivers the eulogy and breaks down on the last line of it. Three months earlier, at John McCain's funeral in Washington National Cathedral, a piece of candy passed between him and Michelle Obama in front of the cameras, and the photograph went everywhere as the decade's chosen image of a man rehabilitated by comparison.
